text.p: Anglo-Dutch consumer products giant Unilever Plc needs to sharpen its focus, co-chairman Niall FitzGerald told Reuters Financial Television.
"We have to be more, sharper in our focus..." he said in an interview on "Inside Equities," scheduled to be broadcast at 1045 GMT/1145 BST on October 17.

FitzGerald, who took over in September, said the business was "very successful" and credited previous management with doing "a fantastic job." But he said the company had to look at its portfolio in the light of changing global circumstances.
"We will judge how we change (the portfolio) based on the ability of individual parts of the portfolio to add real value, economic value, which translates into shareholder value."
Unilever has around 500 companies spanning 90 countries and analysts have speculated it might sell off 20 percent of total businesses in efforts to streamline operations.
Analysts say there could be disposals in Europe coupled with investments in emerging markets such as the Far East.

Since FitzGerald took over as chairman, the company has announced plans to fuse its U.S. businesses Thomas J. Lipton and Van den Bergh Foods under the name Lipton and integrate two units in the Netherlands with the loss of 70 jobs.

At the same time, the group has said it plans to invest at least $100 million in China over the next few years while its DiverseyLever unit has earmarked some $160 million for the Asia Pacific region over the next five years.
FitzGerald said Unilever had been carrying out changes over the last two years but declined to give a timetable for results of the process.
Unilever reported in August that pretax profits were 617 million stg at current exchange rates for the second quarter, down from 655 million stg a year earlier.
